h: פָּרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ, מַאֲמָר ג׳ Parshas HaChodesh — Maamar Gimmel

p: The paytan (in the piyut for the Musaf prayer)
took for the openings of his stanzas
"As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר רִאשׁוֹן לְצִיּוֹן הִנֵּה הִנָּם וְגוֹמֵר
as it says, 'First to Zion: behold, here they are' etc. —
let the Holy One, blessed be He, come
It opened with "Zion is called first,"
"and build the Beis HaMikdash, which is called first."
for the Beis HaMikdash is Zion,
"'Shesiyah' — for from it the world was founded;
our Mishnah follows the one who says
the world was created from Zion" etc.;
from it the beauty of the world was perfected";
is at the place of the Aron in the Beis HaMikdash,
for the view that the world was created from Zion.
as it is written, 'First to Zion' etc."
For the name of Mashiach is called "first,"
since it was created before the world was created,
מִפָּסוּק לִפְנֵי שֶׁמֶשׁ יִנּוֹן שְׁמוֹ [תְּהִלִּים עב, יז]
from the pasuk "Before the sun, his name is Yinon" (Tehillim 72:17).
For the spirit of Mashiach is expounded
"this is the spirit of Mashiach" etc.,
it says that "water" is none other than Torah.
And in truth it is all one,
for the King Mashiach will be
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven
meaning that a stirring of teshuvah will shine forth
in the heart of all Yisrael.
And likewise through Mashiach will come
the full unfolding of Torah she'b'al peh
that the Torah a person learns in this world
compared to the Torah of Mashiach.
And this is "the spirit of Mashiach"
mentioned in the utterance of Bereishis,
which is the beginning of Creation;
is the essence of his life,
for this is what his name is,
as is written in the holy sefarim,
that each person's name is the essence of his vitality,
and therefore when he is called by his name
And this is what they said,
was created before the world was created.
And on this basis the paytan mentioned
at the openings of his stanzas
for in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed
and he mentioned all the expressions of four,
And the root of this is the four cups,
corresponding to the four expressions of redemption:
"And I will take out," "And I will rescue,"
"And I will redeem," "And I will take"
that is, the redemption from the kelipah
that surrounded them on every side in Mitzrayim
and was distressing and oppressing Yisrael.
and afterward, in the blessing after it,
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַאֲמַר הַכָּתוּב [זְכַרְיָה ב, ד]
And this follows the words of the verse (Zechariah 2:4):
"And these have come to terrify them,
to cast down the horns of the nations" etc.
and corresponding to them are four craftsmen to nullify them.
מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף
"Mashiach ben David and Mashiach ben Yosef,
and Eliyahu and the Kohen Tzedek."
the two Mashiachs are both craftsmen
for the building of the Beis HaMikdash;
Eliyahu is a craftsman, for he built an altar;
and Shem is called a craftsman,
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה טִּיבוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם
And we need to understand what Shem has to do,
the builders of the Beis HaMikdash,
being called by the name of Yosef —
means that Yosef clarifies all Yisrael,
"And your people are all tzaddikim" etc.,
and "whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב כג, א)
are called by the name of Yehudah
that David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah —
and so too Mashiach ben David will be
the individual who did teshuvah etc.,
so that deliberate sins become like merits:
"And he was a kohen to the Most High God,"
for then there was not yet revealed
and he was a kohen to the Most High God,
peace be upon him, with this:
"Blessed be Avram to the Most High God" (ibid. 14:19).
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר גַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
And afterward Avraham Avinu too said,
הֲרִימוֹתִי יָדִי אֶל ה׳ אֵל עֶלְיוֹן
"I have raised my hand to Hashem, the Most High God";
and Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, merited
and received from him the kehunah for all generations
And Eliyahu is the last kohen,
and it is stated in Sefer Asarah Maamaros
(מַאֲמַר אֵם כָּל חַי חֵלֶק ג סִימָן כג)
at the site of the altar;
and he wrote that it is possible
that Eliyahu has, from the fund of the Chamber,
(and it was explained in Parshas Shekalim, maamar 2).
to offer outside while the Temple stood,
which was a prohibition punishable by kares,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זִיכָּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה
and nonetheless through this he brought merit
ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים [מְלָכִים א יח, לט].
And this is "First to Zion: behold, here they are,"
and afterward "He gathers in the dispersed of Yisrael"
(as it says in Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 11);
of the building of the Beis HaMikdash and the offerings,
they will nullify the kelipah of the four kingdoms
and then "He gathers in the dispersed of Yisrael."

paragraphs.text: Musaf for Shabbos HaChodesh, Rishon Immatzta, opening stanza and acrostic — “O First One, You strengthened the rose-blossom. Give strength to awaken sleepers from slumber, as You remember the covenant of the first ones.” The seven stanza-opening words mean, in order: First; to Zion; behold; here they are; and to Jerusalem; a herald; I shall give. They reproduce Isaiah 41:27. Their refrains successively name four New Years, four seasons, four periods, four portions, four cups, four kingdoms, and four craftsmen. The verse and the recurring fourfold pattern therefore belong to the original poem itself.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 15:1 — “The Holy One, blessed be He, is called first: I am first and I am last. Tziyon is called first: A throne of glory, exalted from the first, the place of our sanctuary. Esav is called first: The first came out. Mashiach is called first: First to Tziyon, behold, here they are. Let the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called first, come, build the Temple called first, exact payment from Esav called first, and bring Mashiach called first, in the first month.” The Midrash joins Tziyon and the Temple through the verse naming the place of our sanctuary. Rav Tzadok explains their unity through the foundation stone.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 54b — “It was called Shesiyah: a teaching explains that from it the world was founded. Our Mishnah follows the view that the world was created from Tziyon. ... The Sages say: It was created from Tziyon, as it is said, God, Hashem God, spoke and called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting; and it says, From Tziyon, the perfection of beauty—from it the beauty of the world was perfected.” The Gemara preserves several views of creation's starting point. Rav Tzadok follows the view identified with the Mishnah's foundation stone.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 5a — “The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: As reward for three occurrences of first, they merited three firsts: cutting off Esav's seed, the building of the Temple, and Mashiach's name. ... Mashiach's name: First to Tziyon, behold, here they are.” The surrounding discussion concerns first as applied to removing leaven, festival rest, and taking the lulav. Rav Tzadok links these rewards with the firstness proclaimed in HaChodesh.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 54a — “Seven things were created before the world was created: Torah, repentance, Gan Eden, Gehinnom, the Throne of Glory, the Temple, and Mashiach's name. ... The Throne of Glory and the Temple: A throne of glory, exalted from the first, the place of our sanctuary. Mashiach's name: May his name endure forever; before the sun, may his name flourish.” The Gemara's proof for Mashiach's name is from Tehillim 72:17. Rav Tzadok explicitly distinguishes that verse from first to Tziyon.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, on Bereishis 1:2, digital unit 77[1,4] — “Two thousand years of Torah: The spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters, and water is none other than Torah. The face of the waters is its two faces, positive commandments and prohibitions, white and red, right and left. These are the two thousand years of Torah. Two thousand years of Mashiach's days: God said, Let there be light, and there was light.” This is the exact original passage connecting the creation waters with Torah. The manuscript cites Tikkun 36,77b; the digital collection indexes it as unit 77, so its printed coordinate still requires collation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayera 3 — “A person’s vitality is his name, as the holy books write that a father, naming his son, intends the root of the son’s vitality; so one called by name wakes from sleep.” This adds the father’s intent in naming. A name is the root of a person’s life, so Mashiach’s name, made before the world, is his very life.

paragraphs.text: Musaf for Shabbos HaChodesh, Gevuros stanza and Four Seasons refrain — “The month in which salvations encompass, strengthening those who take refuge in Him. ... Four seasons in the year—renew their light as at first! As we have heard, so again hasten [our deliverance], please. Sustain us with rain in the first of the year's months.” The encompassing salvations and the four seasons occur together in the same blessing, providing the exact liturgical wording from which Rav Tzadok develops the image of being surrounded on four sides.

paragraphs.text: Musaf for Shabbos HaChodesh, Hodaah and Sim Shalom refrains — “Let us thresh the four kingdoms, please. ... Four craftsmen, as in the vision: You explained them, one from another, to the seer. As we have heard, so may we again behold; bless us with peace in this month.” The four kingdoms are named in Hodaah; the four craftsmen occur in the following blessing, Sim Shalom, exactly as Rav Tzadok states. Earlier, the Avodah refrain names the four cups. The ellipsis passes from the first line of the Hodaah refrain to the complete Sim Shalom refrain.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 8 — “The three kingdoms stand against the three kelipos of jealousy, desire and honor: Bavel, ‘you are the head of gold’… Persia and Madai against desire… and jealousy and anger against Yavan”; Edom’s evil lies hidden in the depth of its heart. This names which kelipah each kingdom is. It also shows why Edom, the fourth, can be undone only when Hashem uncovers what it hides.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b — “Hashem showed me four craftsmen. Who are the four craftsmen? Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon Chasida's name: Mashiach ben David, Mashiach ben Yosef, Eliyahu, and the righteous priest.” The Gemara gives these four identities. Rashi, quoted next in the discourse, explains the craftsmanship and identifies the righteous priest as Shem.

paragraphs.text: Rashi, Sukkah 52b, s.v. Charashim and VeKohen tzedek — “Craftsmen: artisans. Both messiahs are craftsmen for the building of the Temple. Eliyahu is a stone craftsman, who built an altar on Mount Carmel, and we find that he is destined to be sent. ... The righteous priest: this is Shem son of Noach. He is called a craftsman ... because he built the ark with his father.” Rashi supplies the identification of the righteous priest with Shem and links his craftsmanship to the ark. Rav Tzadok asks how this earlier act belongs with the builders of the future Temple.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 71:2 — “Rachel weeps over her children: Israel are called by Rachel's name, and also by her son's name: Perhaps Hashem, God of hosts, will favor the remnant of Yosef. And also by her grandson's name: Is Ephraim a precious son to Me?” The Midrash traces the collective naming through Rachel, Yosef, and Ephraim. Rav Tzadok relates the Yosef name to the covenantal righteousness clarified by Mashiach ben Yosef.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 98:6 — “Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: All your brothers will be called by your name. A person does not say, I am a Reuvenite, or I am a Shimonite, but I am a Jew.” The Midrash expounds Yehudah, your brothers shall acknowledge you. Rav Tzadok connects the common name Yehudi with David and Mashiach ben David's work of repentance.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 14 — “Shem was the first kohen and taught Torah; he is called a craftsman because he built the Beis HaMikdash in the heart and soul by teaching Torah. Eliyahu is the last kohen.” There Rav Tzadok answers the question another way. Shem builds the Mikdash within, through Torah, and so he is counted among its builders.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 32b — “Rabbi Zecharyah said in Rabbi Yishmael's name: The Holy One, blessed be He, sought to bring the priesthood forth from Shem, as it is said, He was priest to God Most High. When he placed Avraham's blessing before the blessing of God, He brought it forth from Avraham.” The Gemara explains the transfer through the order of Malkitzedek's blessings. Rav Tzadok considers Shem as the earliest priest before the later differentiation of the holy attributes.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Menachem Azariah of Fano, Asarah Maamaros, Eim Kol Chai III:23 — “They said of him that he offers continual offerings in the Temple even though it is desolate, for it stands in its holiness. This accords with what we learned at the end of Eduyos: offerings may be brought even though there is no house. It is possible that funds from the chamber contribution were stored away for him, so that they would be brought from the community's property.” The subject is Eliyahu, identified in the surrounding passage with Pinchas. The author proposes the concealed communal funds as a possibility, not an established historical fact.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 11 — “Why? For thus it is written: Hashem builds Jerusalem, and afterward He gathers Israel's dispersed. Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, was Jerusalem not already built and destroyed? He told them: It was destroyed through your sins, and you were exiled from it. But in the future I shall build it and never destroy it, as it is said, For Hashem has built Tziyon; He has appeared in His glory.” This is the sequence Rav Tzadok quotes. The same digital paragraph begins by stating that Jerusalem is not built until the exiles are gathered, apparently reversing its final clause. That internal textual difficulty requires edition collation; the earlier wording is not silently harmonized here.
